title: Discovery and proof are separate operations
description:
FetchJWTSVID currently collapses discovery and proof into one call: it proves every candidate from every attestor on every request, keeps the single highest-assurance claim, and returns exactly one SVID. That is wrong in three independent ways -- it ignores req.spiffe_id, it contradicts the proto's plural, and once a hardware attestor can prompt it becomes one human touch per candidate per RPC.

This epic splits the three questions a caller actually has into the three surfaces that answer them, and records what that costs. Full decision and rejected alternatives in the design field.
design:
DECISION (Mark, 2026-09-15): discovery and proof are separate operations, and
FetchJWTSVID never prompts a human.

Three surfaces, not one:

  1. "what we may be able to prove" -- a candidate list. Free, silent, no tokens.
  2. "what we have proved"          -- FetchJWTSVID, unchanged on the wire. This
                                       is the proof action; spiffe_id selects
                                       what to prove, hint tags what came back.
  3. "the best thing proved right now" -- not a new call. It is (2) with no
                                       selector and no constraints.

This is the ssh-agent protocol: SSH2_AGENTC_REQUEST_IDENTITIES lists what the
agent holds for free, SSH2_AGENTC_SIGN_REQUEST proves one and may prompt. The
repo already speaks it in hire-attestors/src/ssh.rs. It is also the enumerate()/
prove() seam the Attestor trait already draws, surfaced at the API boundary
instead of collapsed inside fetch_jwtsvid.

REJECTED: return exactly one SVID and make callers declare constraints
(hire_min_assurance et al), refusing when nothing satisfies. Rejected for two
reasons. (a) The information it withholds is obtainable anyway: a consumer
probes with descending constraints and reads the refusals, so the set leaks in
five round trips instead of one. (b) proto/spiffe/workload/workload.proto:139-143
defines `hint` as "guidance on how this identity should be used by a workload
when more than one SVID is returned" -- SPIFFE put the field there for exactly
this case, so the list is the conformant design and the single-SVID answer was
the deviation.

REJECTED: return every entitled identity, proving each. svid is a required
field, so every entry needs a real signed token, so every entry had to be
proven. Once a hardware attestor can prompt, that is one touch per candidate
per RPC -- a FIDO2 tap plus a PIV PIN for a single call. That is consent
fatigue as an attack: ask for everything, let the user tap through, walk away
holding every identity they have. Hence the standing constraint: FetchJWTSVID
returns only what is provable WITHOUT prompting. Touch-gated identities are
reached by asking for them (hire_min_assurance, persona-ouo5.3), which costs
exactly one touch, or by NOT_FOUND.

REJECTED: sort by a single "goodness" scalar. persona-3tly.5 already holds that
presence is at least three independent axes and is not totally ordered, and
assurance-vs-freshness does not collapse either -- a stale iaa3 and a live iaa1
have no honest ordering. So `hint` is NORMATIVE and carries the structure a
caller gates on; the sort order is DOCUMENTED BUT ADVISORY. svids[0] is the
cheap answer; callers that care read the tags. Do not bake the collapse into
the wire format.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, both accepted deliberately:

(1) Surface 1 needs a SECOND gRPC SERVICE on the socket. A candidate has no
token and svid is required, so it cannot ride inside JWTSVIDResponse. The
SPIFFE Workload API itself is untouched and standard consumers never call the
new service -- but "no new wire protocol" becomes "no changes to the SPIFFE
wire protocol", which is weaker than the claim README.md currently makes. Three
open items already want this RPC: `hire enumerate` cheats by building the
registry in-process so it cannot see a running daemon's view, hire-nmh will
need it, and persona-3tly.3 (no surface where a human sees what they are
approving) cannot be built without it.

(2) Surface 3 requires the daemon to HOLD PROOF STATE, which it does not. Today
every request re-proves everything from scratch; the ponytail comment at
hire-grpc/src/service.rs:288 says so and names this cache as the upgrade path.
The wrinkle: proofs are challenge-bound. Claim::derive filters evidence through
Evidence::binds_to(candidate, challenge) and returns None when nothing binds,
which is what makes e2e.rs a_replayed_proof_is_denied pass. Caching a proof
moves its freshness guarantee from CHALLENGE-BINDING ("this signature was made
now, for me") to THE CLOCK ("a signature was made at time T"). That is a
defensible trade and hire_max_age plus the 300s presence TTL are the right
bound for it -- but it is a change to the security model, not an optimization.
If a_replayed_proof_is_denied starts needing an edit, that is the signal the
line has been crossed, not a flaky test.

ORDER: surfaces 2 and 3 first. They use the existing RPC, add no new surface,
and fix the silent-substitution half of persona-5s4b.87. Then the candidate
list and the proof cache together, because the candidate list is only honest if
the daemon can also answer "and here is what I already hold".
